title: EC2 Instance Families, Placement Groups & HPC
summary: Match instance families to workloads and network them for low latency and high throughput.
tldr: Pick the family by the **bottleneck the question names**: CPU-bound → **C**, RAM-bound → **R/X**, local NVMe I/O → **I**, GPU/CUDA or ML → **P/G/Trn/Inf**, spiky light load → **T**.

Placement groups trade blast radius for latency: **cluster** packs instances close for the fastest network, **spread** puts each instance on separate hardware, **partition** gives rack-aware groups for HDFS, Kafka and Cassandra.
Tightly coupled MPI/HPC = **EFA-capable instances in a cluster placement group in one AZ**. Add **AWS Batch multi-node parallel jobs** when you also want a managed queue and scheduler.

keyFacts.text: A **cluster** placement group lives in a single Availability Zone. It gives the lowest latency and highest per-flow throughput, but one AZ failure takes out the whole group.
A **spread** placement group allows at most seven running instances per AZ, each on distinct hardware. Use it for a handful of critical nodes that must not fail together.
A **partition** placement group has up to seven partitions per AZ, each on its own racks. Instance metadata exposes the partition number, so rack-aware software can use it.
**Elastic Fabric Adapter** adds OS-bypass networking for MPI and NCCL, giving lower, more consistent latency than ENA alone. It needs a supported instance type.
**Jumbo frames** work inside a VPC and suit cluster placement groups. Traffic through an internet gateway or a Site-to-Site VPN is still capped at 1500 bytes.

keywords.cue: tightly coupled MPI, lowest inter-node latency
keywords.answer: EFA instances in a cluster placement group, single AZ

keywords.cue: process data in the factory with AWS APIs, AWS maintains hardware
rerunnable cluster spread over AZs, big inter-AZ data transfer bill
keywords.answer: Move the nodes into one AZ in a cluster placement group

traps: A **spread** placement group spreads instances out, so it *adds* latency compared with a cluster group. It is for resilience, not speed.
Spreading HPC nodes across AZs or Regions for "availability" hurts a latency-bound MPI job. Rerunnable HPC belongs in one AZ.
A Batch **array job** runs independent child jobs. Nodes that must talk to each other during the run need a **multi-node parallel** job.
Adding more ENIs does not multiply an instance's bandwidth. Bandwidth is set by the instance type, so move to a larger or newer Nitro type.
A spread group holds at most seven running instances per AZ, so a large rack-aware cluster (dozens of nodes) needs a **partition** group instead.
Jumbo frames do not help traffic that leaves the VPC through an internet gateway or VPN, because those paths carry only 1500-byte packets.
**Outposts** is hardware in *your* building. If the requirement is "no AWS hardware on site" with metro latency, pick a **Local Zone**.
